Senses.Explanation: Literally ‘to deceive people.’ The phrase is accusation, warning, and public-interview vocabulary throughout the Chan record. Yunmen asks for ‘a saying that does not deceive people’ (不瞞人底句), then supplies ‘do not say this is the one that deceives people.’ Miyun writes the maxim ‘deceiving people is no good affair; a good affair does not deceive people’ (瞞人不好事，好事不瞞人). Yet the record also refuses a simple division between deceptive speakers and innocent words. The Blue Cliff Record asks whether the patriarchs and buddhas have an intention to deceive, answers by comparing them to rivers and lakes that have no intention to obstruct, and says that when people cannot pass through, the patriarchs and buddhas consequently ‘become deceivers of people.’ Other records pair deceiving people with deceiving oneself and distinguish being able to do one but not the other. Chan thus bends ordinary deception into a recurrent test of sayings, teachers, hearers, and self-deception while retaining the literal verb; the entry does not decide who intends deception where the text expressly denies such intention.
Senses.Note: 259 raw hits in 125 allowlist texts. ‘Deceive people’ (瞞人) and ‘deceive oneself’ (自瞞) take different objects but retain the same verb sense, so no split is warranted. The intention-denying Blue Cliff passage is preserved because it constrains the definition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖佛還有瞞人之心也無。牙云。汝道江湖還有礙人之心也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk asks whether patriarchs and buddhas have an intention to deceive people; the reply compares this with rivers and lakes having an intention to obstruct.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖佛雖無瞞人之心。自是時人透不得。祖佛却成瞞人去也。不得道祖佛不瞞人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The commentary denies deceptive intention but says inability to pass through makes the patriarchs and buddhas become deceivers; neither side of the text's contrast may be dropped.

Occurrences.Kwic: 瞞人不好事，好事不瞞人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Miyun states the compact maxim: deceiving people is no good affair; a good affair does not deceive people.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汝有一對眼，我也有一對眼。汝若瞞，還自瞞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A master turns attempted deception back as self-deception: if you deceive, you deceive yourself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若只解瞞人，不能自瞞，此人有手無眼；若只自瞞得過，不能瞞人，此人有眼無手
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuzhun's record explicitly distinguishes competence at deceiving people from competence at deceiving oneself.
